transcripts.id:AWeJWnwKSxQAAAAAAAANWg: one of the wildest things that is happening in crypto is bots have wallets now and that's changed a lot in the space so how this flow usually works is that depending on what you have a couple of choices so conventionally right now bots can just talk to themselves either through like a direct message or a slack and you can just get a address from the bot and once you pay it the bot understands okay you made the payment however that is not the idealistic flow because idempotence is a problem you can't match a transfer to a certain invoice essentially what you'd have to do is you'd have to have a special number in decimals at the end which makes it really janky i mean ais don't care but there is definitely a better way to do it so one level up with some infrastructure around this is protocols like x402 these are protocols that orchestrate payments between two bots or even a bot and a human and the way it does this is when the bot basically is talking to another bot if they're talking through the internet a bot that wants payment can request a 402 response which means hey for me to give you this thing i need money first and in that 402 response you have the tracking like what the invoice is you know the amount and you know have all the information to make the payment and then there's a pay server that is watching and seeing if the payment did happen and it marks this as paid or the bot can actually check onchain to see if it was paid and mark it onchain that way so a couple of ways x402 is kind of like the one that is being standardized there's also efforts by circle called nano payments which also basically use the same approach but have a different name on it so yeah depends on what your risk level is and experimentation level is you can go really simple and make the bot stock directly or you can use one of these payment protocols

transcripts.id:AWeJWnwKSxQAAAAAAAANWA: that one stuck bridge transaction can cost a whole trade and here's one example of how that can happen. So let's say you are a searcher, you are trying to find a very fast execution for trading. So what you want to do is you have Ethereum on the source chain. So what you want to do is you want to take your Ethereum and you want to deposit in Solana, but in a specific vault and that vault, you see some arbitrage opportunity that you can sell that vault token for a higher spread than what you would get if you were to deposit. So there's some arbitrage there, your starting token is Ethereum, it's on Ethereum, your ending token is some vault token on Solana, and you need to get there and you need to get really, really fast. So what you would do is you would first create a swap, depends on if you have an Ethereum bridge or not, but if let's say you don't have an Ethereum bridge because there's no native bridge between Ethereum and Solana. So let's say you want to do a swap first. So you're going to swap your Ethereum into USDC, then you're going to bridge. You have a couple of choices. If you use a free cheap path like CCTP, it's going to take you 15 minutes. If you use a faster path, it's going to cost you a little bit more money, but you have to do the math there and then you have to do a destination bridge and then on the bridge, then you have to take the USDC and swap it into Solana probably, and then that Solana you need to deposit into a vault, then you need to get that LP token and actually sell that. And you do this very fast before the arbitrage opportunity goes away. But what happens if that bridge transaction gets stuck? Well, now you're in a bind because your starting tokens were Ethereum, your target token was an LP token that is actually native to Solana, which is a wrapped Solana variant. So you have Ethereum on the source side, you needed Solana, but you're stuck with USDC and the arbitrage opportunity is now gone. So what do you do? These are the kind of execution gaps that we have in onchain routing today that, yeah, if you're running small shops and you're doing trades with very small frequency like yeah, you can probably absorb it and it doesn't lose anybody's lunch. But if this goes into enterprise level skill, then you're going to literally start losing people's lunch. And that's why it's very important for that bridge transaction to not fail.
